writeup: TIC 447112476 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 0.7055 days. The primary eclipse causes the system to dim by 0.82 percent, detected with a signal-to-noise ratio of 114.8 using automated analysis of TESS photometry. No secondary eclipse was detected. Pixel-level image analysis confirmed a signal-to-noise ratio of 5.1, though the centroid offset of 6.8 arcsec from the target warrants consideration. The candidate does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, making it a previously unlisted source. The machine-learning screening score of 0.66 indicates moderate confidence that this represents a real stellar system. All automated data quality checks passed without flags, supporting the validity of this candidate for further study.
